resolution: Resolved: current state voter guide and municipal notices confirm October 16 postmark; same-day registration is a separate in-person route.
Resolved: online same-day registration continues through November 3, but late registrants must vote in person. A generic five-days-before rule was not used.
Resolved: state registration instructions and Ballotpedia confirm the October 9 postmark rule.
Resolved: October 24 application receipt, not merely postmark; separate electronic-delivery deadlines are explained.
Resolved: applications must be filed by October 27. Current official guidance retains the court-ordered ballot postmark grace period; older static calendar wording was superseded.
Resolved using original SurveyUSA PDF: fieldwork October 8–12, original release October 13, 718 likely voters, 45–42.
Resolved using Suffolk methodology: October 8–11; 500 likely voters; ±4.4 points.
Resolved using original toplines: 561 likely voters; ±4.9 credibility interval, distinct from 800 adults and ±4.03.
Resolved by replacing the stale UVA House mirror with the original October 16 Cook ratings and checking all 435 districts against DDHQ.
Closed by exclusion: no national early-vote count is asserted or imported. A single-source number is not needed for a defensible forecast, and is not relabeled verified.

Resolved for the published finance scope: both Texas Senate nominees’ 2026 authorized-committee receipts, disbursements and cash through September 30 reconcile with OpenFEC and secondary figures. Three committee records were summed; an auxiliary-fund termination label was distinguished from the principal committee. Unreconciled figures elsewhere remain excluded.

Resolved for the published ordinary-domestic calendar: all 51 request, in-person voting, return and poll-hour summaries compared across source documents; local variation is explicit. Unverified uniform opening times and portal availability are not asserted.
Resolved: all three conditional dates and office scopes rechecked; Louisiana House versus Senate systems distinguished.
Resolved: legislative, executive, judicial and measure watch entries added. Unsupported court/measure winner probabilities are explicitly unforecasted.
